name: Film and TV trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about films, television, animation, actors, directors, from any decade. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Who directed the 1997 film Titanic?
items.explain: Titanic was written and directed by James Cameron, who won the Best Director Academy Award for it.

items.question: How many Academy Awards did Titanic win at the 1998 ceremony?
items.explain: Titanic received fourteen nominations and won eleven, including Best Picture and Best Director.

items.question: Titanic was the first film to pass which worldwide box-office milestone?
items.explain: Britannica notes that Titanic was the first film to gross over $1 billion.

items.question: Who directed the 1972 crime film The Godfather?
items.explain: The Godfather was directed by Francis Ford Coppola, who co-wrote it with Mario Puzo.

items.question: Which star of The Godfather won the Best Actor Academy Award for his performance in the 1972 film?
items.explain: Brando won Best Actor. Pacino, Caan and Duvall were nominated in the Best Supporting Actor category.

items.question: The Godfather film is based on a novel by which author?
items.explain: The film is based on Mario Puzo's novel The Godfather, and Puzo co-wrote the screenplay.

items.question: Who directed the 1975 thriller Jaws?
items.explain: Steven Spielberg directed Jaws, which was released in 1975.

items.question: Who composed the famous score for Jaws?
items.explain: John Williams composed and conducted the Jaws score for Steven Spielberg's film.

items.question: Who wrote and directed the original 1977 Star Wars film?
items.explain: Star Wars (later titled A New Hope) was written and directed by George Lucas.

items.question: Which actor provided the voice of Darth Vader in the original Star Wars?
items.explain: David Prowse wore the Vader costume, but George Lucas chose James Earl Jones for the voice.

items.question: Which actor played Luke Skywalker in the original Star Wars trilogy?
items.explain: Mark Hamill was cast as Luke Skywalker for the original 1977 Star Wars.

items.question: Which actor played the smuggler Han Solo in the original Star Wars?
items.explain: Harrison Ford played Han Solo, who teams up with Luke Skywalker to save Princess Leia.

items.question: Which actress starred as Dorothy Gale in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz?
items.explain: Judy Garland played Dorothy Gale and became internationally known for the role.

source.title: The Wizard of Oz (1939 film) - Wikipedia

items.question: Which song from The Wizard of Oz won the Academy Award for Best Original Song?
answers: If I Only Had a Brain
We're Off to See the Wizard
items.explain: "Over the Rainbow", with music by Harold Arlen, won the Academy Award for Best Original Song.

source.title: The Wizard of Oz (film) | EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: What is the name of Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz?
items.explain: Dorothy tries to save her dog Toto from Miss Gulch before the tornado carries them to Oz.

source.title: The Wizard of Oz (film) | EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: Who wrote the 1900 novel that the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz was adapted from?
items.explain: The film was adapted from L. Frank Baum's novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.

source.title: The Wizard of Oz (film) | EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: What is the name of the coffeehouse where the group hangs out in the sitcom Friends?
items.explain: Central Perk is the coffeehouse frequented by the group, and Rachel works there as a waitress.

items.question: Which actor played Ross Geller in Friends?
items.explain: David Schwimmer played Ross Geller, whose on-and-off romance with Rachel Green runs through the series.

items.question: Which instrument does Phoebe Buffay play when she sings at Central Perk?
items.explain: Phoebe plays acoustic guitar and sings her simple, awkward songs at Central Perk.

items.question: How many seasons did the sitcom Friends run for?
items.explain: Friends ran from 1994 to 2004 and finished its ten-season run with 236 episodes.

items.question: Who created the animated sitcom The Simpsons?
items.explain: Matt Groening, who grew up in Portland, Oregon, created The Simpsons.

items.question: What is the most commonly used address of the Simpson family home?
items.explain: The most commonly used address for the Simpsons' house in Springfield is 742 Evergreen Terrace.

items.question: Where does Homer Simpson work as a safety inspector?
items.explain: Homer works as a safety inspector at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant.

items.question: Which friendly, devout Springfield resident in The Simpsons is known for using the word "diddly"?
items.explain: Ned Flanders is a devout, compassionate pillar of the Springfield community, and "diddly" is one of his trademark words.

items.question: Which TV network produced the fantasy series Game of Thrones?
items.explain: Game of Thrones was created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss for HBO.

items.question: Game of Thrones is based on the book series A Song of Ice and Fire by which author?
items.explain: The series adapts George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novels.

source.title: Game of Thrones - Simple English Wikipedia

items.question: Game of Thrones is set on Essos and which other fictional continent?
items.explain: The series is set on two imaginary continents, Westeros and Essos.

source.title: Game of Thrones - Simple English Wikipedia

items.question: Which actor played Walter White in Breaking Bad?
items.explain: Bryan Cranston played Walter White, a high-school chemistry teacher who starts making methamphetamine after a cancer diagnosis.

items.question: Under which alias does Walter White become a drug kingpin in Breaking Bad?
items.explain: Walter Hartwell White is also known by his alias Heisenberg.

items.question: In which US city is Breaking Bad set and filmed?
items.explain: Breaking Bad is set and filmed in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

items.question: Which 1995 film was the first fully computer-animated feature film?
items.explain: Toy Story, Pixar's debut feature, was the first computer-animated feature film.

source.title: Toy Story | Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

items.question: In Toy Story, what kind of toy is Buzz Lightyear?
items.explain: Buzz is a shiny new astronaut toy that Andy receives for his birthday, which makes Woody jealous.

items.question: What is the name of the boy who owns the toys in the original Toy Story?
items.explain: The film follows a roomful of toys and their owner, a young boy named Andy.

source.title: Toy Story | Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

items.question: Who directed the 1960 horror thriller Psycho?
items.explain: Psycho was produced and directed by Alfred Hitchcock.

items.question: Which actor played the shy motel owner Norman Bates in Psycho?
items.explain: Anthony Perkins played Norman Bates, who runs the Bates Motel with his domineering mother.

items.question: Which actress played Marion Crane, who is murdered in Psycho's famous shower scene?
items.explain: Janet Leigh played Marion Crane, an embezzler who is killed while she showers.

items.question: Which actor played the title role in the 1994 film Forrest Gump?
items.explain: Tom Hanks starred as Forrest Gump and won the Best Actor Academy Award for the role.

items.question: Who directed Forrest Gump?
items.explain: Forrest Gump was directed by Robert Zemeckis, who won the Best Director Academy Award for it.

items.question: Forrest Gump follows the life of a man from which US state?
items.explain: The film follows an Alabama man named Forrest Gump and his experiences in 20th-century America.

items.question: Which fairy-tale heroine starred in Walt Disney's first full-length cel-animated feature, released in 1937?
items.explain: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) was the first full-length cel-animated feature film.

source.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film) - Wikipedia

items.question: Disney's 1937 Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was based on a fairy tale by which writers?
items.explain: The film is based on the German fairy tale "Snow White" by the Brothers Grimm.

source.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film) - Wikipedia

items.question: Along with one full-size statuette, how many miniature Academy Awards did Walt Disney receive for Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs?
items.explain: The Honorary Academy Award for Snow White was one full-size Academy Award statuette and seven miniature ones.

items.question: Which actor played Harry Potter in all eight films of the film series?
items.explain: Daniel Radcliffe played the title character in all eight Harry Potter films from 2001 to 2011.

items.question: Which school of magic does Harry Potter attend?
items.explain: Harry attends Hogwarts, where Albus Dumbledore is headmaster and he befriends Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger.

items.question: How many films make up the Harry Potter film series?
items.explain: The series has eight films, from Philosopher's Stone (2001) to Deathly Hallows – Part 2 (2011).

items.question: Which actress played Hermione Granger in the Harry Potter films?
items.explain: Emma Watson was selected to play Hermione Granger, alongside Daniel Radcliffe and Rupert Grint.

source.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (film) - Wikipedia

items.question: Who directed all three films of The Lord of the Rings film trilogy?
items.explain: Peter Jackson directed all three Lord of the Rings films and co-wrote the screenplays.

source.title: The Lord of the Rings (LOTR) | Britannica

items.question: Which actor played the wizard Gandalf in The Lord of the Rings films?
items.explain: Ian McKellen played Gandalf, appearing opposite Elijah Wood's Frodo.

source.title: The Lord of the Rings (LOTR) | Britannica

items.question: Where must Frodo take the One Ring in order to destroy it?
items.explain: Frodo is tasked with taking the Ring to Mount Doom, the only place where it can be destroyed.

source.title: The Lord of the Rings trilogy (film) | EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: The Lord of the Rings films are based on novels by which author?
items.explain: The trilogy was adapted from J. R. R. Tolkien's Lord of the Rings novels, published in the 1950s.

source.title: The Lord of the Rings trilogy (film) | EBSCO Research Starters
